bottleneck: De-extinction via genome editing produces approximations, not resurrections: a mammoth-elephant hybrid lacks the mammoth's microbiome, learned behaviors, epigenetic programming, and Ice Age ecosystem. Editing dozens of traits into an elephant genome risks developmental failure, since the interactions between edits are untested, and the resulting animal is a novel organism with unknown welfare needs. The ecological niche it would fill no longer exists, raising the question of what de-extinction is actually for.
current_state: Colossal Biosciences has produced edited 'dire wolf' proxies and mammoth-trait mice. No de-extinct species walks the earth; ecological and welfare questions are unresolved and largely undebated.

title: De-extinction produces approximations, not species
why_it_blocks: Billions flow toward resurrecting the past while the genetics cannot deliver the animal that was lost — only a hybrid in an ecosystem that no longer exists. The bottleneck is conceptual, not just technical, and the spending diverts from conserving living species.
